half-buried-slope.what_is_exposed: Top, primary bedding face and right side; approximately lower 0.15 m intersects soil.
half-buried-slope.before: Regular rectangular top/side and repeated raised lamina offsets stay obvious above soil.
half-buried-slope.after: Asymmetric outline helps local-fragment placement. Broad exposed cap/right planes and straight parallel color laminae remain visible.
half-buried-slope.seam_or_teaching_block: Abrupt soil/rock material contact and deliberate cut planes remain; burial does not repair them.
half-buried-slope.use_conclusion: A plausible way to place a local rock fragment, with unresolved style quality. Bedding is visible from ordinary-height perspective, not only from above.

embedded-bank.what_is_exposed: Primary bedding face, exposed top/right rim; rear overlaps neutral bank.
embedded-bank.before: Looks like a rectangular teaching slab inserted into soil wall.
embedded-bank.after: Outline is less rectangular, but hard boundary and contact shadow still read as a separate inserted fragment. Smooth color bands remain conspicuous.
embedded-bank.seam_or_teaching_block: No seamless geological transition is claimed. Remaining boundary/cut-fragment feeling is part of the evidence.
embedded-bank.use_conclusion: Local insert/exposure can be compared. Continuous natural cliff or repeated terrain-tile use is not established.

response_to_user_concern: The user objection to programmatic parallel side bands remains valid for this candidate. Terrain placement changes visibility, not the underlying layer construction or surface material quality. Await further style direction; no model revision authorized by this evidence supplement.
